clue_prompt: Find the joints each animal bends before pushing off. What changes when it lands?
core_parts: Hip, thigh bone, knee, shin bones, ankle, toe bones and muscles.
operations: Muscles pull the bones through the joints. Straightening the leg pushes against the ground.
traits_attributes: Both hind legs bear weight and generate thrust for movement.
scale_medium: Both work on land. Leg length and leverage affect stride and takeoff.
input_output: Energy in food → muscle contraction → movement and heat.
flow_direction: Both bend to absorb load and straighten to push off.
modification_exemption: A hopping rabbit typically pushes off with both hind legs together. A cat normally alternates them when walking.
blind_spot_note: The joint that looks like a backward knee is the ankle. The actual knee is closer to the body.

clue_prompt: Look for the bones both wings hide. What makes the broad surface?
core_parts: Shoulder, upper arm, forearm, wrist, digits and flight muscles.
operations: Wingbeats move air and help generate lift and thrust.
traits_attributes: Both are vertebrate forelimbs adapted for powered flight.
scale_medium: Air is the working medium. Wing area matters relative to body mass.
input_output: Energy in food → muscle work → moving wings and air.
flow_direction: The downstroke usually supplies much of the force. Wing shape also changes on the upstroke.
modification_exemption: A bird uses feathers for much of its wing surface. A bat stretches skin across elongated fingers.
blind_spot_note: Both are called wings, even though powered flight evolved independently in the two lineages.

clue_prompt: Which stationary part lets both panels swing?
core_parts: A panel, a hinge pin, hinge leaves and a fixed frame or post.
operations: The panel pivots around the hinge axis while the frame or post stays still.
traits_attributes: Both create or block a passage with a rotating barrier.
scale_medium: Solid hardware carries the load. Wide panels put more leverage on the hinges.
input_output: A push or pull → hinge rotation → an opening or closing passage.
flow_direction: The same hinge guides opening and closing in opposite directions.
modification_exemption: The gate is often anchored to a post and leaves room for outdoor drainage and ground clearance.
blind_spot_note: The names tell you where the barrier is used. Both can use the same hinge principle.

clue_prompt: What moves closer together when your hands squeeze the handles?
core_parts: Two arms, two handles, two working ends and a pivot.
operations: Squeezing the handles rotates both arms around the pivot and closes the working ends.
traits_attributes: Both trade handle travel for force at the working ends.
scale_medium: Solid tools pass force through a pivot. Longer handles can increase leverage.
input_output: Hand force → pivoting arms → force against material.
flow_direction: Handles close to cut or grip and open to release.
modification_exemption: Scissor blades slide past each other. Ordinary plier jaws press toward each other.
blind_spot_note: Cutting and gripping sound unrelated until you trace the same pair of levers.

clue_prompt: What do both have to push out of the way to keep something above the water?
core_parts: A body or shell, a low-density interior and an outer surface in contact with water.
operations: Water pushes upward with a force equal to the weight of the water displaced.
traits_attributes: Both float when they can displace enough water to support their total load.
scale_medium: Water is the medium. Available displacement limits the load that can float.
input_output: Weight presses down → water is displaced → buoyant force acts up.
flow_direction: N/A — Same Direction. Buoyancy acts upward in both.
modification_exemption: A hull makes an enclosed or sheltered air volume. A foam jacket keeps buoyant material close to the wearer.
blind_spot_note: The boat carries a load. The jacket supports a wearer. The water applies the same rule.

clue_prompt: Where must the blocker sit for either shadow to reach you?
core_parts: A light source, an opaque blocker and a surface or observer in the shadow.
operations: The blocker interrupts some light paths, creating a region that receives less direct light.
traits_attributes: Both can have a darker center and a softer edge when the light source has apparent size.
scale_medium: Light crosses air or space. Apparent size and alignment determine the shadow.
input_output: Light source → blocker interrupts part of the beam → reduced direct light behind it.
flow_direction: Light travels from the source toward the shaded region in both.
modification_exemption: A solar eclipse uses the Moon, whose apparent position must align with the Sun from the observer's location.
blind_spot_note: An eclipse has its own name because of its astronomical scale. The blocking pattern is a shadow.

clue_prompt: What flat part helps each seed stay in the air longer?
core_parts: A seed and a light wing that interacts with moving air.
operations: As the seed falls, the wing makes it spin and slows its fall compared with a similar unwinged seed.
traits_attributes: Both give wind more time to carry a seed away from the parent plant.
scale_medium: Air is the medium. Wing shape and seed mass affect the fall.
input_output: Gravity starts the fall → wing interacts with air → slower descent and wind drift.
flow_direction: The seed falls while wind may move it sideways.
modification_exemption: The maple wing is part of a fruit. In many pines the wing is associated with the seed released from the cone.
blind_spot_note: Maple helicopters and pine seeds sound like different inventions. Rotation is the shared pattern.

clue_prompt: After rain, what decides which way both channels carry water?
core_parts: A bed, banks, flowing water and land that drains toward the channel.
operations: Gravity carries water downslope while the flow can move sediment and shape the channel.
traits_attributes: Both collect runoff and may also receive groundwater.
scale_medium: Water flows over land. Channels vary in width, depth and discharge.
input_output: Rain, runoff and groundwater → channel flow → water and sediment downstream.
flow_direction: N/A — Same Direction. Water follows the downstream gradient in both.
modification_exemption: Creeks are usually smaller in local usage. There is no universal width at which a creek becomes a river.
blind_spot_note: Names often reflect local geography. Size alone does not define a new flow mechanism.

clue_prompt: Start at the lamp and trace the energy backward. Where do the paths differ?
core_parts: A lamp or LED, a circuit and a source of electrical energy.
operations: Current through the lamp produces light and some heat.
traits_attributes: Both turn electrical energy into light you can direct.
scale_medium: Electrical current runs through a circuit. Light leaves into the surrounding air.
input_output: Hand motion or battery chemistry → electrical energy → light and heat.
flow_direction: Energy flows toward the lamp once either light is switched on.
modification_exemption: The crank turns a small generator. The battery flashlight draws from energy already stored in its cell.
blind_spot_note: The names point to where energy starts. The light at the end comes from an electrical circuit.

clue_prompt: Which part first catches sunlight, and what keeps the device useful later?
core_parts: Photovoltaic cells, a rechargeable battery and charging electronics.
operations: The solar cells make electricity in light, and charging electronics store some energy in the battery.
traits_attributes: Both can keep supplying power after sunlight fades while the battery has charge.
scale_medium: Sunlight reaches semiconductor cells. Panel area limits power under the same light.
input_output: Sunlight → electricity → stored battery energy → light or power to a device.
flow_direction: Charge flows into the battery during charging. The battery powers a load during use.
modification_exemption: The garden light powers its own lamp. The power bank supplies a charging port.
blind_spot_note: One gets named for what it lights, and the other for what it charges. They can share the same input and storage.

clue_prompt: Follow oxygen to the blood. What keeps the two media close without mixing them?
core_parts: Thin gas-exchange surfaces, nearby capillaries and a way to keep water or air moving.
operations: Oxygen diffuses toward blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses out across the exchange surface.
traits_attributes: Both use a large surface and a short diffusion distance.
scale_medium: Irrigated gills exchange gases with water. Lungs exchange gases with air.
input_output: Oxygen-rich water or air → diffusion → oxygen in blood and carbon dioxide leaving it.
flow_direction: Water usually passes across fish gills. Most mammals move air in and out along the same airways.
modification_exemption: Gill filaments meet flowing water. Mammalian alveoli are enclosed in the lungs.
blind_spot_note: Breathing and gill ventilation look different from outside. Diffusion drives exchange in both.

clue_prompt: Count which chambers receive blood and which chamber or chambers push it out.
core_parts: Two atria, ventricular muscle, valves and blood vessels.
operations: Contraction raises pressure and sends blood onward. Valves guide flow.
traits_attributes: Both are muscular pumps with separate atria receiving returning blood.
scale_medium: Liquid blood is the medium. Pressure and flow vary with vessel resistance.
input_output: Returning blood and muscle energy → contraction → blood flowing to exchange surfaces and tissues.
flow_direction: Atria receive blood before ventricular contraction sends it out.
modification_exemption: An adult frog has one ventricle. A human has separate right and left ventricles.
blind_spot_note: Heart diagrams can suggest that every vertebrate uses the same number of chambers.

clue_prompt: How does the spinning driver make the second wheel spin?
core_parts: An input shaft, an output shaft and two rotating members linked by contact or by a belt.
operations: A driver transfers torque to a follower. Relative diameters affect the speed ratio.
traits_attributes: Both can change rotational speed and torque.
scale_medium: Solid wheels and shafts carry load. The belt also bends around its pulleys.
input_output: Input shaft rotation → torque transfer → output shaft rotation.
flow_direction: An open belt turns its pulleys the same way. A pair of external gears turns opposite ways.
modification_exemption: A smooth belt relies on friction and can slip. Meshing gear teeth engage directly.
blind_spot_note: The belt is easy to notice and the shafts are easy to miss. The shafts do the comparable work.

clue_prompt: Where do the brake pads touch the rotating wheel assembly?
core_parts: A control lever, a force linkage, pads and a rotating braking surface.
operations: The pads squeeze the running surface. Friction slows the wheel and releases heat.
traits_attributes: Both resist rotation with force applied at a radius from the hub.
scale_medium: Metal braking surfaces and friction material carry load and dissipate heat.
input_output: Hand force and wheel motion → pad friction → heat and slower rotation.
flow_direction: In both, friction opposes the rotation of the braking surface.
modification_exemption: The rim is the braking surface in one system. The other uses a separate rotor at the hub.
blind_spot_note: Rim and disc name the part that gets squeezed. Both rely on pad friction.

clue_prompt: Why can both place an upside-down image on a screen?
core_parts: An object, light paths, a barrier or optical element, and an image surface.
operations: A pinhole selects narrow bundles of rays. A lens bends broader bundles toward image points.
traits_attributes: Both can form an inverted real image on a sensor or screen.
scale_medium: Light is the medium. A pinhole can trade brightness against blur and diffraction.
input_output: Light from the scene → selection or refraction of rays → image on a screen.
flow_direction: Light travels from the object through the aperture or lens to the image surface.
modification_exemption: The pinhole blocks most rays. The lens collects more light and has to be focused for a chosen distance.
blind_spot_note: A camera can form an image before it has a glass lens. The useful question is which rays reach each point.

clue_prompt: What changes when you push the same distance on a liquid versus a gas?
core_parts: Cylinders, pistons, seals and a confined working fluid.
operations: A pressure difference exerts force on a piston. At the same pressure, more piston area yields more force.
traits_attributes: Both convert pressure effects into forces on moving surfaces.
scale_medium: Hydraulics generally use a low-compressibility liquid. Pneumatics use a compressible gas.
input_output: Input force or pressure → fluid pressure → output force and motion.
flow_direction: Moving a piston one way can increase pressure and drive another piston. Releasing pressure can let it return.
modification_exemption: Gas compresses appreciably and can act springy. Liquids usually transmit a stiffer response.
blind_spot_note: In physics, both liquids and gases are fluids. The names tell you which kind is doing the work.

clue_prompt: What forces can move water upward through small channels and pores?
core_parts: Connected wettable passages, water and surfaces that attract it.
operations: In a towel, surface tension and wetting draw water into pores. In xylem, evaporation from leaves helps pull continuous water columns.
traits_attributes: Both depend on water interacting with surrounding surfaces and with itself.
scale_medium: Water is the medium. Effective channel size matters, while plant height also requires tension-driven transport.
input_output: Water supply → porous pathway or xylem → wet material or water delivered to leaves.
flow_direction: A towel can wick in any direction away from its supply. Xylem sap commonly moves from roots toward leaves.
modification_exemption: Leaf evaporation maintains the pull in a working plant. A towel can wick without leaves or living cells.
blind_spot_note: Water rising in a towel gives a useful starting model. A tall tree also needs the pull created by transpiration.

clue_prompt: What determines whether water vapor collects as liquid drops or as ice crystals?
core_parts: Moist air, a cool surface and water vapor near that surface.
operations: Vapor condenses into droplets on a sufficiently cool surface. If conditions favor ice, vapor can deposit directly as crystals.
traits_attributes: Both transfer atmospheric moisture to a surface and release latent heat.
scale_medium: Air carries vapor. Surface temperature and local saturation help determine the phase.
input_output: Water vapor → cooling and phase change → droplets or ice.
flow_direction: In both, water moves from the air to the cooler surface.
modification_exemption: Dew is liquid. Direct-deposition frost forms as solid ice, without first making liquid dew.
blind_spot_note: People also use frost for frozen dew. This card compares dew with frost that forms directly from vapor.

clue_prompt: Trace the energy across the shaft and the wires. Which is the input?
core_parts: Conductors, a magnetic field, a rotating part and a shaft in common rotary designs.
operations: Current in a magnetic field can produce torque. Motion that changes magnetic flux can induce voltage.
traits_attributes: Both couple mechanical motion and electrical energy through electromagnetism.
scale_medium: Electrical current travels in circuits, and rotation occurs in a mechanical assembly.
input_output: Motor: electrical energy → shaft work. Generator: shaft work → electrical energy. Both lose some energy as heat.
flow_direction: Their dominant energy direction is reversed.
modification_exemption: The difference is which side supplies energy. Some machines can work in either mode with suitable controls.
blind_spot_note: Motor and generator describe jobs. One design can sometimes perform both.

clue_prompt: Follow the sunlight. What reaches the outlet on each device?
core_parts: A sun-facing collector surface and a path to carry away usable energy.
operations: A photovoltaic cell separates charge carriers. A thermal collector transfers absorbed heat to a liquid.
traits_attributes: Both capture solar radiation and provide less output when usable sunlight falls.
scale_medium: Light reaches each collector. Wires carry electricity and pipes carry heated fluid.
input_output: Sunlight → electricity in the photovoltaic panel, or sunlight → heat in water or a heat-transfer fluid.
flow_direction: Energy moves from sunlight to the collector and outward to a load or storage.
modification_exemption: The photovoltaic collector produces electricity at its terminals. The thermal collector delivers heat.
blind_spot_note: Both are called solar panels. The output connection tells you which one you have.

clue_prompt: What concentration pattern is sustained when neighboring streams run in opposite directions?
core_parts: Adjacent passages, barriers for selective exchange, and flows in opposite directions.
operations: Gill countercurrent exchange keeps an oxygen gradient along much of the surface. Kidney loops use different permeabilities and salt transport to build an osmotic gradient.
traits_attributes: Both use opposing flows to make gradients useful over the length of a structure.
scale_medium: Water, blood and tubular fluid are liquid media. Diffusion or active transport depends on the tissue.
input_output: Fish: oxygenated water → oxygen in blood. Kidney: tubular salt and water handling → a gradient that supports water conservation.
flow_direction: Opposite directions occur in both. The exchanged substance and physiological job differ.
modification_exemption: A gill exchanges oxygen between streams. The kidney loop multiplies an osmotic gradient using segment-specific transport.
blind_spot_note: Countercurrent names a layout. Exchange and multiplication describe different jobs that layout can support.

clue_prompt: How does the same mineralized tissue carry load as a shell and as an interior lattice?
core_parts: A collagen-rich matrix mineralized with calcium phosphate, living bone cells and spaces for vessels or marrow.
operations: Cortical bone carries load in a dense layer. Trabecular struts and plates carry load through an open network.
traits_attributes: Both resist loads and remodel in response to mechanical and biological conditions.
scale_medium: A dense shell and a porous lattice place solid material differently for a given bone shape.
input_output: Applied load → stress distributed through mineralized tissue → support and small deformation.
flow_direction: Cortical shells and trabecular networks both carry their share of applied loads. There is no fixed flow direction.
modification_exemption: The difference is the arrangement and amount of open space, not a switch to a different basic material.
blind_spot_note: Spongy describes architecture. Individual trabeculae are solid bone tissue.

clue_prompt: Which pump traps a volume, and which adds speed to a moving liquid?
core_parts: An inlet, an outlet, a driven moving element and a housing.
operations: A piston displaces a trapped volume. A centrifugal impeller adds velocity and the casing helps convert part of it to pressure.
traits_attributes: Both convert shaft or actuator work into liquid flow against resistance.
scale_medium: Liquid is the working medium. Flow rate, pressure rise and viscosity influence pump selection.
input_output: Mechanical work → pressure and motion in liquid → discharged flow.
flow_direction: Liquid goes from inlet to outlet in both. A piston chamber alternates intake and discharge strokes.
modification_exemption: The piston pump uses a repeating chamber volume. The centrifugal pump feeds liquid continuously through an impeller.
blind_spot_note: The word pump describes the delivery. The way liquid gains energy determines how the device behaves.

clue_prompt: How can one design keep its input and output on the same axis?
core_parts: Toothed wheels, shafts or carriers, and supports that maintain tooth engagement.
operations: Teeth pass torque between moving members. Tooth counts and any held member set the speed relation.
traits_attributes: Both can trade greater output torque for lower output speed, with losses.
scale_medium: Solid tooth contacts transmit load. Planet gears can share loads when the set is designed for it.
input_output: Input torque and rotation → tooth contact → output torque and rotation.
flow_direction: Two external gears rotate oppositely. A planetary set's relative directions depend on which member is held and which is driven.
modification_exemption: A planetary set has planets on a moving carrier around a sun gear, often inside a ring gear.
blind_spot_note: Both use meshing teeth. The arrangement of axes and moving members explains their different packaging.

item_b_label: Air-Source Heat Pump in Heating Mode
clue_prompt: Which side of the cycle is the appliance designed to make useful?
core_parts: Compressor, evaporator, condenser, expansion device and circulating refrigerant.
operations: Refrigerant evaporates to absorb heat and condenses to release heat. Shaft or electrical work drives the cycle.
traits_attributes: Both use work to move heat from a lower-temperature region to a higher-temperature region.
scale_medium: The refrigerant changes phase. Heat moves between the refrigerant and indoor or outdoor air through heat exchangers.
input_output: Work and heat absorbed at the cold side → circulation and compression → heat delivered at the warm side.
flow_direction: Refrigerant cycles through the same stages. The useful heat transfer is at a different side.
modification_exemption: A refrigerator values heat removed from its cabinet. A heat pump in heating mode values heat delivered indoors.
blind_spot_note: Cooling and heating name the result the user wants. They can come from the same thermodynamic cycle.

clue_prompt: If every dimension doubles, how do self-weight and member cross-section change?
core_parts: A deck, truss members, joints, bearings or supports, and load paths.
operations: Triangulated members route forces to supports. Compression members may buckle and tension members stretch.
traits_attributes: Both use geometry to distribute forces, and both depend on material and connection behavior.
scale_medium: At geometric similarity with the same material, weight scales with length cubed and area with length squared.
input_output: Self-weight and traffic or test loads → member forces → reactions at supports.
flow_direction: Loads pass through deck and truss to the supports in both.
modification_exemption: A full-size bridge cannot be validated by simply enlarging the model. Self-weight, buckling, connections and service loads have distinct scaling constraints.
blind_spot_note: The model can copy the outline closely while missing the prototype's stress and stability margins.

clue_prompt: Where does the water travel long enough to lose sediment or nutrients?
core_parts: Vegetation, soil or substrate, microbial communities and a pathway for water.
operations: Flow slows, particles settle or get trapped, and plants and microbes can retain or transform some nutrients.
traits_attributes: Both can reduce some pollutants when water has enough contact with active surfaces.
scale_medium: Water moves over or through wet soil and vegetation. Performance depends on flow, residence time and design.
input_output: Runoff or controlled inflow → settling, contact and biological processes → altered outflow.
flow_direction: A treatment wetland often has a designed inlet and outlet. A stream buffer commonly intercepts runoff moving toward a stream.
modification_exemption: The treatment wetland routes water through a deliberately designed treatment area. A buffer is a strip positioned along a waterway.
blind_spot_note: The word wetland names a habitat or treatment setting. Buffer names a position and protective role.

clue_prompt: Can a drop land on one side of a ridge and later reach the other basin underground?
core_parts: Two drainage regions, a boundary and gradients that guide water.
operations: Surface runoff follows topography. Groundwater follows gradients in hydraulic head through connected pores or fractures.
traits_attributes: Both describe where neighboring flow paths diverge.
scale_medium: The surface route lies over land. The subsurface route depends on permeability, recharge and hydraulic head.
input_output: Precipitation → runoff or infiltration → discharge to a stream, spring or other outlet.
flow_direction: Water moves away from the divide toward different outlets, although groundwater divides can shift.
modification_exemption: A surface divide normally follows higher ground. A groundwater divide follows the local hydraulic head field and may shift with pumping or recharge.
blind_spot_note: The same word divide marks a flow boundary. A ridge on a map cannot always locate the underground one.

clue_prompt: When charging stops, what physical state keeps the energy available?
core_parts: A storage medium with two accessible states, a reversible energy conversion path and electrical controls.
operations: A pump raises water to store gravitational energy. Battery charging transfers lithium ions and stores energy in electrochemical states.
traits_attributes: Both charge, retain energy, and later deliver a smaller amount of electrical energy because of losses.
scale_medium: Pumped storage depends on water volume and elevation difference. Batteries depend on active materials, cell count and operating limits.
input_output: Electricity → raised water or electrochemical energy → electricity during discharge.
flow_direction: The net conversion reverses during discharge. Water descends, and lithium-ion motion reverses relative to charging.
modification_exemption: The reservoirs store energy through elevation. Battery electrodes store it through chemical and electrical state.
blind_spot_note: Calling a reservoir a battery describes its grid function. The medium holding the energy is different.

clue_prompt: Which side makes hydrogen, and which side consumes it to power a circuit?
core_parts: In common membrane designs, electrodes, a catalyst and an ion-conducting separator.
operations: Electrolysis uses electrical work to split water. A fuel cell uses an electrochemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen to supply electrical power.
traits_attributes: Both move ions internally and electrons through an external circuit.
scale_medium: Water and gases move through separate paths. Ions cross the internal electrolyte.
input_output: Electrolyzer: water and electricity → hydrogen and oxygen. Fuel cell: hydrogen and oxygen → electricity, water and heat.
flow_direction: The overall chemical and useful electrical energy directions reverse across the two devices.
modification_exemption: Electrolysis consumes electrical power. A fuel cell supplies it. Practical units may use different materials and controls.
blind_spot_note: The overall reactions are related. That does not make every commercial device reversible.
